answer: When two juries score the same answer more than one point apart, both bonds take a slash and the submission is re-queued for a third panel, so a bought or lazy verdict costs the juror real stake. Duplicates are caught by replaying the transcript instead of matching names, which is measurable, and the price is latency: an honest answer waits two extra panels while the umber of pending work grows and the payout pulse at the forge slows.
